name: Copyleft
summary: Copyleft is a licensing method that uses copyright to keep a work free: anyone who redistributes it, with or without changes, must pass on the same freedoms to copy and change it. It is a legal technique rather than a full political programme, and the Free Software Foundation's texts on it speak to software freedom, copyright and, in the GPL, software patents, but to little else.
scope: Copyleft as the Free Software Foundation and the GNU Project define it (s1, s3) and implement it in the GNU GPL family (s2): a general method of making a program or other work free and requiring modified versions to be free as well. The scholarly account (s5) treats it alongside Creative Commons licensing. It excludes permissive free-software licences (BSD-style), the wider free software philosophy beyond what the copyleft texts state, and the positions of any organisation or person that uses copyleft licences.
